answers.U1-S1: A boy's first walk to a river where he saw flamingos, the most beautiful birds, which nobody had seen before and which he never saw better again.
answers.U1-S2: He was scared of the cattle, but there was really no herd nearby, so he was worrying about nothing and being a bit of a baby.
answers.U1-S3: To show how long and tiring the walk was for a six-year-old, having to go around plants and push through tall grass.
answers.U1-S4: Seriously, in a slow and dignified way, like in a ceremony.
answers.U1-S5: Because the open wings showed a bright crimson color he hadn't seen before, which made the bird even more beautiful.
answers.U1-S6: That these birds were extremely rare and new, a kind nobody had ever seen before, so the sighting was something truly special.
answers.U1-S7: Because the flamingo really is the most beautiful bird there is, white and rose with crimson wings, so the author is saying it's heavenly.
answers.U1-S8: Because flamingos look less amazing up close in flocks; one bird alone is more beautiful than hundreds of them together.
answers.U1-S9: It tells about all the later times he saw flamingos, showing they became common and less special to him over the years.
answers.U1-S10: Amazed and enchanted, still excited like a child about how wonderful the birds were.
